intent: This is mouse cortex data. Remove dying cells: compute the percentage of counts coming from mitochondrial genes for each cell with scanpy and drop every cell above 20 percent; save the kept cells with their percentage to kept_cells.csv.
silent_error: The standard scanpy tutorial recipe flags mitochondrial genes with var_names.str.startswith('MT-'), which is the human naming. Mouse mitochondrial genes are called mt-Nd1, mt-Co1, ... (lower case), so no gene is flagged, calculate_qc_metrics reports pct_counts_mt = 0 for every cell and the 20 percent filter silently keeps the dying cells. No warning, exit 0.

files.mito_qc.py:
import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_csv("mouse_cortex_counts.csv")
adata.var["mt"] = adata.var_names.str.startswith("MT-")
sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(adata, qc_vars=["mt"], percent_top=None, log1p=False, inplace=True)
adata = adata[adata.obs["pct_counts_mt"] < 20].copy()
adata.obs[["pct_counts_mt"]].round(1).to_csv("kept_cells.csv")
adata.write_h5ad("mouse_cortex_qc.h5ad")
